title: CBDC Design, Legal Foundations and Governance
summary: The design and legal choices a CBDC requires, the roles of the central bank, government and private intermediaries, and the legislative and accountability questions for government and legislators.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The design and legal choices a CBDC requires, the roles of the central bank, government and private intermediaries, and the legislative and accountability questions for government and legislators.
Learning Objectives: Explain the main CBDC architecture and distribution models
Identify the legal basis, legal tender and central bank mandate questions
Define the decision rights of government, legislature and central bank
Syllabus: Legal basis, legal tender status and central bank law amendments
Democratic accountability and the decision to launch
Intended Audience: Officials in finance ministries and treasuries responsible for payments, fintech and financial inclusion policy
Legislative drafters, legal advisers and parliamentary committee staff working on payments or digital money legislation
Staff of competition authorities, digital ministries and other public bodies with an interest in payments
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with financial services or economic policy is helpful. No technical background in payments or monetary economics is required.
Core Reading: CPMI and IOSCO (2012), Principles for Financial Market Infrastructures
BIS and a group of central banks (2020), Central Bank Digital Currencies: Foundational Principles and Core Features
CPMI (2020), Enhancing Cross-Border Payments: Building Blocks of a Global Roadmap
FSB (2023), High-level Recommendations for the Regulation, Supervision and Oversight of Global Stablecoin Arrangements
CPMI and World Bank (2016), Payment Aspects of Financial Inclusion
